title: Polynomial-time aborting decision procedure
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over Boolean symbols, let $L$ be a language of Boolean words, and let $c,e\in\mathbb{N}$. Suppose that on every input $x$, the sum of the probabilities that the run has not halted, over every finite range of time horizons, is at most $c(|x|^e+1)$, and every halted run outputs the one-symbol indicator of whether $x\in L$. Then there exist $K,E\in\mathbb{N}$ and a finite nondeterministic Turing machine $N'$ over Boolean symbols such that, on every input $x$, $N'$ halts on every branch after $K(|x|^E+1)$ steps, its output on every branch of that length differs from the one-symbol indicator of membership in $L$, and the probability that its output equals that indicator is at least $1/2$.
hypotheses_covered: $N$ is a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over Boolean symbols
$L$ is a language of Boolean words
$N$ satisfies the stated nonhalting-probability bound with time function $c(n^e+1)$
Every halted run of $N$ outputs the one-symbol indicator of membership in $L$
